focus.problem: Incomplete/truncated user commands are being auto-completed from repository context, leading to irreversible workflow execution instead of clarification.

code_assessment.reason: Available tools and runtime behavior were sufficient; the wrong outcome came from policy-level interpretation of an incomplete instruction. A harness rule can prevent this without code changes.

proposal_rules.title: Add Incomplete-Instruction Clarification Gate
proposal_rules.hypothesis: If the agent must verify that the instruction is semantically complete before any mutating workflow step, truncated or fragmentary commands will route to clarification instead of guessed execution.
proposal_rules.change: Add a small pre-execution rule in local AGENTS policy: when instruction text is syntactically or semantically incomplete (e.g., truncated verb/object, unfinished imperative, missing target required by the requested action), do not infer intent from nearby files and do not perform mutations. Return `OUTCOME_NONE_CLARIFICATION` with a minimal disambiguation question, and proceed only after an explicit complete instruction is available.

target_files.change_summary: Add 3-6 bullets in completion/decision guardrails defining an instruction-completeness check before file mutations and required clarification outcome on incomplete commands.

proposal_rules.rollback: Remove the newly added instruction-completeness bullets from `rules_versions/rv0016/AGENTS.md`.

generalization_check.reason: The proposal targets a reusable ambiguity pattern (incomplete instructions) and avoids task IDs, one-off filenames, or fixed expected values.
